In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a progressive development of benzodiazepine‐receptor binding and of GABA‐concentration in the human brain, with the highest concentrations in the cerebellum, the lowest in the frontal cortex, and an intermediate concentration in the occipital cortex.

benzodiazepine binding sites and free GABA concentrations in the brain are both high in the foetus, fall during the neonatal period and then rise again during infancy to reach adult levels by the age of 2 years, whereas the concentration of the other amino acids studied remains relatively constant throughout development.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benzodiazepine binding site is present in the human brain before the end of the second trimester of foetal life, and that it increases in density during the third trimester.
the development of the benzodiazepine and GABA systems in the human cerebral cortex and cerebeller cortex are closely related and parallel the development of the other amino acids.
the concentration of GABA is very low in foetal brain, rises sharply at birth and reaches the adult value by about 2 years of age.

benzodiazepine binding is a useful tool for the study of the developing brain.
